quests.title: Into the Wind, Into the Frigid North

dialogue.t: And just like that, we're in Snezhnaya! Feels like we only just left Nod-Krai.
Remember back in Nasha Town, how all our friends came to see us off before we left?
The day's finally come. We're off to meet the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya! What is she planning, and why does she need the Gnoses? Soon, we'll have our answers.
Guess this'll be the "end of your journey" that your sister(your brother) mentioned... What is she(he) expecting you to find there?
*sigh* Snezhnaya still feels like a long way away. Hopefully, there'll be plenty of time to relax, eat some good food, and have fun before we arrive.
...But whenever Paimon gets thinking about how our destination is right around the corner, all these questions come flooding into Paimon's head. It makes her so nervous...

dialogue.sit: It's sure been a long time coming.
I'm a little nervous too.

dialogue.t: Yeah... Anyway, enough about all that. We can't start the final leg of our journey with that kind of mindset!
Just think — we've fought dragons and sea monsters, defeated creations of the gods, faced prophecies of doom and the threat of the Abyss... Heck, we've even been to the moon.
With all that experience under our belts, how could we be any more prepared?

dialogue.sit: Great point. Thanks for the pep talk.

dialogue.t: Sure thing! Now, stick close to Paimon, the best guide you could ever ask for, and let's charge straight for the finish line! Off we go!
What about me? Do I get a callout?
Whoa! Columbina? You kinda snuck up on us there...

dialogue.sit: How did you know I was here?
I don't think I told anyone...

dialogue.t: D—Don't look at Paimon! Paimon didn't sell you out this time!
Oh, so it was you! Alright, guess there's no hiding it now.
All your friends have gathered at The Flagship to see you off.
I invited Sandrone too, but she said she had to go back to Snezhnaya. She must be busy.
She had some nasty things to say about you before leaving. Would you like to hear them?
Ugh, she hasn't changed a bit. Alright, let's hear it...
"If they're heading to Snezhnaya, I'll bet it's to cause trouble for Her Majesty the Tsaritsa. Attending a farewell party for people like that would not be a good look for me right now."
"Also, please tell them not to count on getting help from a Fatui Harbinger in Snezhnaya."
"Our time working together was... not terrible, precisely, but we're on different sides. So when you get there, don't do anything to make life difficult for both of us."
Well, that definitely sounds on-brand for her. The attitude, the reasoning... Alright, we'll do our best to keep our distance then.
No, you've misunderstood. I think she means that she'd like you to go see her.

dialogue.sit: Uh... How'd you figure that?

dialogue.t: As long as you don't make things difficult for both of you, you'll be fine.
Huh. You really have to read between the lines with Sandrone...
Go on, get to the The Flagship — everyone should be there by now. I told Lauma that you once treated me to a truly unforgettable meal...
Today, I want to return the favor. It's... my gift to you.
Hehe, it's definitely nice to be treated. But hopefully by this point, you know that you don't owe us any favors.

dialogue.sit: Yeah, friends don't keep score.
I'll come back to visit.

dialogue.t: Mm. The moon of Nod-Krai will always give you a warm welcome.

dialogue.sit: Time flies when you're having fun, enjoying delicious food with friends, and reminiscing about past adventures.
After a lovely meal filled with laughter and warmth, it's time to start the next chapter of your journey.

dialogue.t: Wow, pure white as far as the eye can see! It's so pretty... Come on, keep up!

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: Let's see how your Kamera skills are these days... Whoa, wait a sec, Paimon sees something.
Come on, quick! It looks like a train carriage!
Paimon's heard that Snezhnaya has loads of railways and trains. This must be one of them! But... why is it abandoned?
It's still so cold...

dialogue.sit: Still feeling chilly from getting buried in the snow?

dialogue.t: Dunno... maybe? Also, is it just Paimon, or is the snow getting heavier?

dialogue.sit: This never happened in Nod-Krai.
If you're cold, come a little closer.

dialogue.t: Yeah. So it can't just be because of the cold...
Ugh... It's hard to describe, but Paimon feels so weird... She's never felt like this before.
Everything feels heavy... Getting kinda dizzy, too...

dialogue.sit: Should we turn back?

dialogue.t: Oh, no need. Paimon's just feeling a little low on energy, that's all. It's nothing serious. Not worth ruining our travel plans over.

dialogue.sit: Well, don't push yourself, okay?
If you start feeling worse, tell me right away.

dialogue.t: Yep, sure thing! Snezhnaya, here we come!

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: Incoming entity detected. Authorization... granted. Initiating original...
Hello, Transcend... Descender, who has reached the eve of Tomorrow. Eye of Graeae, at your service.
Time since last activation: ... Time measurement unavailable due to the influence of... Anyway, it must have been a very long time.

dialogue.sit: Um... What are you?

dialogue.t: I am, uh... I was born to fulfill a mission: to reach Tomorrow.
To this end, I must... I must... Strange, what was it...? Wait, my body...
Huh? Why is my body like this?

dialogue.sit: I was about to ask you.
Oh... so you weren't born like this?

dialogue.t: Apologies. After a long period of inactivity, it appears that a lot of data has been lost.
Anyway, I was created so that humanity could reach Tomorrow... But I am unable to load further details at this moment.
Nevertheless, serving humanity remains my primary objective. I have detected a drop in your surface body temperature. You cannot remain active in this state for much longer...
In accordance with my preset programming, upon reactivation, I must ask the one who awakened me the following question:
Will you accept me, Transcender? I will assist you, protect you, and fulfill my mission until we reach Tomorrow...

dialogue.sit: Uh, no thanks. This is all a bit too strange for me...
I will accept you.

dialogue.t: I understand your position. However, given your current physical condition, I must suggest that you reconsider.
Before I was activated, you called out a name. Presumably that of your missing companion?
If you agree to accept me, after helping you get out of here, I will search for said companion and pinpoint their location.

dialogue.sit: ...Really? You can do that?

dialogue.t: To answer your question: Yes.

dialogue.sit: ...Then I accept.

dialogue.t: You have made a very wise decision.
Now that we have reached an accord, you will be my new user. May I ask your name?

dialogue.sit: {NICKNAME}.

dialogue.t: Very well. I will remember this name until the mission is complete.

dialogue.sit: What is your mission, exactly?

dialogue.t: I need to... I need to recover my body, retrieve the power to unlock Tomorrow, and help the suffering masses to reach the far shores where the Empty Ark floats...
I can sense my power scattered across this ice-covered land. I even have a vague sense of where it might be found... But right now, that is not essential.
The key right now is you. You must survive and reunite with your companion.
Scanning local environment... Exit has been sealed off with ice...

dialogue.sit: Maybe we can use Pyro?

dialogue.t: That would not be an efficient approach. One moment... Usable Construct Blueprint detected nearby...
You can use this to clear the solid ice ahead of you more quickly.
Kresnik Kristall located. Please collect at your earliest convenience.
The recent construct you built provides highly efficient heating by utilizing the unique properties of Kresnik Kristall.
Unfortunately, Prime Ice Constructs have a very short lifespan and cannot be stabilized during the development period. Hence, the authorization to use Kresnik Kristall was granted.
...That said, I have already forgotten what warmth feels like.

dialogue.sit: Maybe when you get your body back...

dialogue.t: Yes. Perhaps then, we can warm ourselves by the fireside together.
But for now, all you need to remember is this: If you collect Kresnik Kristall, I can extract the energy within and use it to maintain your body's surface temperature.
Approaching the target location. Scanning for signs of life... Lifeforms detected: ...Two?

dialogue.sit: Does that mean someone else is there besides Paimon?

dialogue.t: Affirmative — however, that is not the reason for my confusion. According to my database, this location is a train station, meaning the number of lifeforms is unusually low.
Real-time environmental data suggests that the train station may no longer be in use. But whatever the situation, please exercise caution.

dialogue.sit: Let's head inside and take it from there.
Paimon!
...Who are you?

dialogue.t: Don't worry. She's only sleeping.
You must be {NICKNAME}. She called your name repeatedly while attempting to battle her way through the blizzard.
Newcomers to Snezhnaya struggle to adapt to the sheer cold at the best of times. Lately, even the locals are suffering, with a powerful monster having summoned a bitter snowstorm.
You two must be very important to one another. You should take more care not to get separated.

dialogue.sit: Your eyes... are you... Khaenri'ahn?

dialogue.t: There are indeed some Khaenri'ahns left in this world who survived the cataclysm. But I doubt that is news to you.
It would be unwise to interrogate my identity here. Focus your attention on your travel companion instead.
We will meet again very soon.
The unidentified subject has now left the area. He appears to be an individual of great significance, but my search has yielded no relevant data. I will try searching the database again...

dialogue.sit: I have a rough idea...
He's probably some big shot who works for the Tsaritsa.

dialogue.t: Against the odds, your companion is safe and sound. The other person even left a blanket for her.

dialogue.sit: I'll boil some water.

dialogue.t: *groaning*...
Ah, {NICKNAME}! Thank goodness you're okay! Paimon was so worried. She looked everywhere for you... *coughing*!

dialogue.sit: It's okay, take it easy. Are you feeling alright?

dialogue.t: Um, pretty much the same as when we first got to Snezhnaya... Paimon must've caught a cold. She was feeling so faint, she just couldn't keep going any longer, so she had to lie down and sleep it off...
Wait... Where did The Jester go?

dialogue.sit: "The Jester"? That was The Jester?

dialogue.t: Yep, the Director of the Fatui, "The Jester" Pierro. So you met him?

dialogue.sit: Yeah, we spoke briefly...
But he didn't reveal his identity.
(The Jester must know everything about the Tsaritsa's plans, but there's no way he'd tell me just like that. We might well have ended up clashing...)
(Hmm... Well, he was right about one thing. Right now, the most important thing for me is to take care of Paimon while she's unwell.)

dialogue.t: He had no intention of explaining his motives, and he left in something of a hurry.
Eek! What the... who was that!?

dialogue.sit: Oh, I found this in an ice cave.

dialogue.t: It looks like a... pair of goggles. How amazing... A self-aware, talking pair of goggles...

Snezhnaya was once the land of the fae. There are many ancient creations here that I'm sure would broaden your mind further still. Mind you, my database is also expanding as we speak — you must be a rare creature yourself.

dialogue.sit: The Eye of Graeae helped me find you.
That's how I made it safely out of that cave.

dialogue.t: Oh, wow! Well, thank you so much! You've earned yourself some of Paimon's favorite candy! ...Oh, but by the looks of it, you probably can't eat that, can you?
Goodwill detected. Instead of candy, perhaps I can suggest my preferred strategy: Please clean me regularly to keep me operating at peak efficiency.
Hehe, that makes sense — every pair of goggles needs wiping clean once in a while. Sure thing, Mister!
Anyway, back to The Jester for a second. Paimon's still confused about something...
When he first showed up, he already knew Paimon's name — and he acted like he expected Paimon to know who he was, too...
Paimon could tell that he was Khaenri'ahn from his eyes, and he definitely seemed like someone pretty important. But beyond that, Paimon didn't know anything about him.
It was only later, after he rescued Paimon from the snow, that he properly introduced himself. That's the only reason Paimon knows he was The Jester.

dialogue.sit: So he knows you?
Is that why he was here? He came looking for you?

dialogue.t: Seems unlikely... He ran into the snow following the sound of Paimon's voice with a really anxious expression on his face. He didn't act like someone who knew she would be here in advance...
And after bringing Paimon here, he just stared out at the snow. He didn't do anything to Paimon at all. In fact, he barely said anything. Wouldn't even answer any of Paimon's questions, either.
Paimon didn't feel unsafe around him, and he didn't seem to have any ulterior motives. For all we know, he might have just ignored Paimon's questions so she'd give up and go to sleep...
Please allow me to interrupt. "Fatui" and "Director" are unfamiliar terms. May I ask for clarification?
Wait, you've seriously never heard of the Fatui? Huh. They're like, uh... the Tsaritsa's inner circle. Really powerful people. And the Director is their boss!

Understood. Since they hold elite positions and serve their god directly, it stands to reason that they would conduct themselves with due decorum. I am inclined to agree with your assessment, Miss Paimon: I did not detect any ill will from the gentleman in question.

dialogue.sit: I see what you mean.
We'll remember to thank him next time we see him.

dialogue.t: *coughing*...

dialogue.sit: Sorry, I shouldn't have encouraged you to talk so much...
Paimon, new plan. Let's get out of Snezhnaya for now. We can come back after the weather clears up and you're all better.
The Jester mentioned that this snowstorm, being the work of a monster, is worse than most. Even if we made it to Snezhnograd, we'd still have to wait out the storm before we could do any exploring.

dialogue.t: Aw... Well, it's really nice of you to look out for Paimon, but... *cough* she doesn't wanna hold you back...
We were really psyched up for this journey when we first set off. Just think of all the burning questions we have... If we turn back now, who knows how long it'll take before we finally get answers?
Further information is required regarding the monster situation. But objectively speaking, there is another, more pressing issue at hand.
At this point, we have traveled a significant distance into the blizzard. Were we to turn back now, the road would be extremely treacherous — especially since we would need to travel on foot.
If, however, we continue onward, there may be a better solution.
Do you remember what I said as we neared this location? I told you that this is a train station. While it has evidently fallen into disuse for unknown reasons, the tracks remain intact.
We can break through the blizzard and forge ahead by driving a train. That is the Snezhnayan way.
There is a small town up ahead, which would be the perfect place for Miss Paimon to rest and recover.
Paimon thinks Goggles here makes a great point, hehe. Let's do that!

dialogue.sit: Are you sure you're up to this? I don't want you to push yourself.

dialogue.t: Ah, c'mon, don't worry! Think of all the traveling we've done so far — when has Paimon ever gotten sick before? Practically never, 'cause she's in great shape! Sure, she's a little tired right now, but it's sure to clear up on its own.

dialogue.sit: Fair enough.
We'll stay the night in the town, then take it from there.

dialogue.t: Affirmative. Should you ever need my assistance during your future adventures, please call for the "Eye of Graeae" whenever you wish.
Otherwise, I will remain silent to avoid causing any unnecessary distraction. Now, please follow me to the train tracks.

dialogue.sit: You meet up with Paimon in the house...

dialogue.t: Heading north from here, we will soon arrive at...
Wait, there's an error message... "Could not detect clear tracks"...?
Um, what exactly does "clear" mean...?
Brace for impact, friends! Preparing to enter impromptu flight mode...

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: How strange. Not only was the station's status different from my records, but even the railroads and the terrain itself have changed substantially...

dialogue.sit: Paimon, are you okay?

dialogue.t: Yeah, thanks to your quick reflexes...
My sincere apologies for putting you in danger. I'm afraid I'm as confused by all this as you are...

dialogue.sit: We need to find a way to update your databanks...
Shame about the train.

dialogue.t: Agreed — this is likely a consequence of outdated railroad data. The discrepancies between the old data and present reality are far greater than I anticipated...
Fortunately, our crash landing has at least brought us much closer to the town. According to the data, anyway.
Your data had better be right this time...
I can assure you, it certainly is. Please look this way, and you will see a Kresnik's Torch.
It seems our ill-fated train ride was a blessing in disguise. We have taken the shortest possible route.

dialogue.sit: It wasn't what you'd call comfortable, though...

dialogue.t: Rest assured that I will take user preferences into account next time I plan a route. Next time, I will get it right...

quests.description: Finally, you and Paimon prepare to set off for your next stop, Snezhnaya…

quests.title: Gunfire in the Silent Lands

dialogue.sit: You meet Alyosha at Sretomorozsk and successfully repair the train.

dialogue.t: Paimon's just gonna stay here and get some good rest. You guys be careful out there!

dialogue.sit: Hi there. Do you know if there are any inns still taking guests in this town?

dialogue.t: Doubt it. They're probably all closed. No one has enough Kresnik Kristall to heat their own homes, let alone a business.
*sigh* What a bummer...
I clocked you a while back. You adventurers, or something? We don't get many tourists in inland Snezhnaya these days.
Why's that? Because of the snowstorm?
In part, but the bigger reason's Project Stuzha. Since it's Her Majesty's will, we have to put up with it whether we like it or not.

dialogue.sit: I don't really know what Project Stuzha is.

dialogue.t: Oh, sorry. I assumed it was common knowledge by now. Basically, the Tsaritsa is planning something big — something that requires an enormous amount of energy.
Even if they used all the surplus Kresnik Kristall in Snezhnaya, it still wouldn't be enough to meet demand.
So, the Veche passed a resolution requiring all factories and households to reduce their energy consumption. The policy has been charmingly named Project "Stuzha," meaning "bitter cold."
Bitter cold? So like... "It's gonna be a cold winter, folks — you're all gonna have to find a way to get through it." That kind of idea?
Pretty much. When you're broke, you scrimp and save. When it's cold, you huddle together for warmth. There's always a way to stretch things out to make ends meet...
Trouble is, if you stretch someone out like an elastic band for too long, who knows if they can ever bounce back... *sigh* You know what? Come with me, and see for yourself.
Can you please explain to me why the price of Kresnik Kristall has gone up by a third again, even as our purchase quota's gone down?
You only come here twice a month! This won't even last us a week!
The supply and pricing of Kresnik Kristall are based on current production volumes and price data.
We Fatui are only responsible for delivery and security. I'm not in a position to explain to you how the figures are calculated, but I assure you they are as fair and reasonable as possible.
Oh, so our lives mean nothing to you? How can you expect anyone to survive a single night in this weather without heating!?

Since you insist on making me repeat myself every single visit, I will remind you again: There is no monopoly on the trade of Kresnik Kristall. You are free to purchase the shortfall from elsewhere on the market.
What market? Nobody else is selling — and when they do, they charge eight times the normal rate! It's robbery, is what it is!
Which is why the Snezhnograd Veche passed a resolution to support border communities — without which, you wouldn't even be able to buy Kristall from us to begin with.
So if you're here just to argue, move aside and let the next person in line come forward. Everyone's feeling the cold here.
You... You...!
Alright, everyone, let's calm down for a second. A few words, if I may. We're all subjects of Her Majesty the Tsaritsa, and I'm sure every one of us is dedicated to her great cause.
We all know how cold it is, and the more it snows, the harder life gets. Everyone's struggling already — let's not make things even more difficult for each other.
But Liaison Shishkin, there's clearly something wrong with this quota! I have a family in Morepesok who tell me they can buy at least double our Kristall allotment.

Oh, believe you me, I had the same reaction when I first saw the numbers... Couldn't believe what I was reading. I even wrote a letter to confirm the true figures, but... *sigh* I'm afraid the quota really is as low as you've been advised.
Still, you must understand that calculating these energy quotas is a complicated balancing act. They have to factor in population, town size, industrial application...

Our top priority must be to keep the largest Kresnik's Torch burning continuously. Only then can we sell the remaining Kristall for household use, and in doing so, we must make sure that everyone is treated fairly.
As our Fatui comrade said, they are only responsible for delivering the goods. They need to keep accurate records, and they do not have any authority to modify the rates or quotas.
That's right. Our duty is to do things by the book.
*sigh*...
...Tell you what. Listen, I know how anxious and upset everyone is. As a matter of fact, I was just discussing it with the mayor.
What we can do is open the lower combustion chamber of the Kresnik's Torch to the public. You can come to me directly to register, and I will allocate time slots accordingly.

I can't guarantee there'll be ample energy for household use. But we can at least make sure you'll be able to boil water and cook food each day. Let's hang in there and make this work together, alright?
Fine. I don't see any alternative...
So this is Project Stuzha in action, huh... No wonder nothing's open for business. People are barely getting by.

dialogue.sit: It seems like there's nothing we can do...
So, where do we go from here?

dialogue.t: You were looking for an inn, right? For your, uh... fae friend?
Oh, Paimon's not a fae, hehe. Just Paimon. She must've caught a cold or something. We only just got to Snezhnaya, and we're still getting used to the climate...
I have a small place in Sretomorozsk. I don't stay there very often, though, so it's pretty basic.
But if you're not picky, you're welcome to rest there for now. It's not much, but I've got blankets and a warm fire.
Are you sure? That's really kind of you...

dialogue.sit: Thank you so much. This is an enormous help.

dialogue.t: Alright then. This way.
Ohh, so cozy and warm... Paimon's getting nice and toasty.
Oh, wait, Paimon only introduced herself so far, didn't she? This is Paimon's best friend, {NICKNAME}.
Good to meet you. I'm Alyosha.
Most travelers find the Snezhnayan climate to be a shock to the system at first. But as long as you keep yourself warm, you should be fine.
Still, you should keep an eye on your condition. When people are too quick to dismiss a cold, it can easily end up turning into something more serious.
Don't say that! Paimon's too young for chronic health issues...

dialogue.sit: Is there a doctor in Sretomorozsk?

dialogue.t: They aren't in town right now, and they won't be back anytime soon. The train station has been closed ever since these power shortages began.
I do a lot of hunting, so I spend most of my time exposed to the elements. But even the animals wouldn't survive long in a storm like this, let alone a hunter.
Nothing to do but sit tight in town until the weather improves.

dialogue.sit: Is there any possibility of getting the train station running again?

dialogue.t: I get that you're in a hurry, but even if the station were open, that doesn't mean there'd be any trains. We could end up stuck here for a long time, I'm afraid...

dialogue.sit: Actually... I, uh, have my own train.

dialogue.t: What? Your own train? Wait, hold on... THAT train? The one that suddenly fell out of the sky and crash-landed on the ice?
Hehe, we got lucky and found it in a cave. ...Then our luck ran out, and we had a little accident.

dialogue.sit: I'd really like to get to Snezhnograd and find a doctor.

dialogue.t: Pretty crazy for a random find in the mountains... Well, as long as your train's good to roll, you might get to Snezhnograd after all.
I've been doing some digging recently. Turns out, the real reason for the current energy crisis in Sretomorozsk is that some of the supply is being seized for a private stockpile.
But to expose what's going on, I need to catch them in the act. So, I'm heading off to catch a rabbit.
Huh? Wait, a rabbit stole the Kristall?
...It's a figure of speech. Real rabbits couldn't pull this off. They'd prefer carrots to Kresnik Kristall anyway.

dialogue.sit: Do you have a suspect in mind?

dialogue.t: Shishkin. Mr. "Positive Attitude, Let's All Get Along, Now Shall We?"
Him, really? Paimon never would have guessed...

dialogue.sit: I'll come with you. Let's go.

dialogue.t: Huh? You're coming with?

dialogue.sit: Solving the energy crisis will help get the station running again.
Then we can go to Snezhnograd.

dialogue.t: Ah... O—Okay then, just give Paimon a second to get ready—

dialogue.sit: You stay here and rest, Paimon.
We don't want your condition getting any worse.

dialogue.t: Alright, guess there's no point pushing myself. Paimon will stay here and hold the fort, then.... Be careful, you two!
Oh yeah, there's one more introduction to do. Tugarin, get in here.
Aww, a doggie!
Woof woof!
Oof, angry doggie... Tugarin doesn't like being petted, then?
He likes to think he's above that kind of thing. He's my hunting partner, so he'll be joining us when we head out.
"Carrots" aside, we'll need to stay completely undetected. We can't risk spooking our rabbit, or there's no telling which burrow he'll scurry back into.
First, we need to find a way into the train station and see if we can find any real freight data. Shishkin's figures can't be trusted.
Then, we get Tugarin to catch a scent and find out which way the Kristall went...
...What are you eating?
Check it out. When you're all out of carrots, try jerky!
Woof, woof, woof!
Good doggie, good doggie!
A fellow dog lover, huh?
Yup! And rabbit-lover! Carrots are great too, y'know!
...Good to know. Eat up, Tugarin. We got a lot of work to do.

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: There we go: a freight list. Straight from the Fatui, so Shishkin won't have had the chance to doctor the figures.
Looks as new as the day it was printed. I guess no one bothers reading these unless they have ulterior motives.

dialogue.sit: If they did, there'd be no loophole for him to exploit.

dialogue.t: Yeah, this is all we need. C'mon, let's get out of here, then go track down the Kristall.

dialogue.sit: How do we do that?

dialogue.t: Tugarin's a keen hunter, and catching rabbits is his specialty.
This must be the rabbit's warren. Good job, boy.
Sure enough, there's a tunnel. You stay here and keep watch — I'm gonna take a look inside.

dialogue.sit: With the investigation complete, you and Alyosha secretly notify the Fatui and recover some of the missing Kristall.
Thanks for looking out for us. *sigh* Things are getting tougher by the day.
Tellingly, the entrance to the tunnel is right at Shishkin's residence. Now, it's time to confront him.

dialogue.t: Hang tight for a moment. This old lady... she doesn't really know who's who anymore.
Wh? Ah... grandson. It's so cold today, you must be freezing...
Ma'am, it's me, Alyosha.
Alyosha? ...Alyosha who?
You know me... I came by earlier today. Cleaned the ashes out of your stove, gave you some warmer bedding, and washed your back.
Oh... Uh...
...I'm sorry, I don't remember.
Now, how often do I get to see my grandson, hmm? Come on, take a seat and relax while I fix you something to eat.
It's okay, you just rest. I'm fine.
Oh, you. It's nice to come and visit your old granny once in a while, isn't it? Sretomorozsk's a good town. All sorts of things to do and people to meet, and the local officials are good to us...
Sit down, come on, take a seat. I still have some fruit left. Let me get it for you.
Please, don't get up on my account, you need to rest... Where's the fruit?
Right under the basket by the door. Um... or maybe it was on the bedside cabinet...
Well, grandson dear? Do you like it?
Very much, Ma'am. It's delicious.
Good, good... Wonderful...
You don't need to save anymore for me next time, alright? Fresh fruit is hard to come by at the moment. You should eat it as soon as you get it.
Oh, I don't need it. I'm fine. But if you like it, come back for some more soon.

dialogue.sit: After a long chat, Alyosha tidies up the old lady's room before finally leaving, still holding the bag of long-spoiled berries in his hand.

dialogue.t: Some kind soul must've given these to her. But she always saves the nicer things for special occasions.

dialogue.sit: How do you know her?

dialogue.t: I met her at the market back before her health began declining. She was a lovely old lady. We're from the same hometown.
Not many people have heard of Alatyr — and if they have, it's usually for all the wrong reasons... there's a gang of highwaymen that came from there.

Now that it's an abandoned village, it's rare to find anyone who shares fond memories of our hometown. So after we got talking and realized we were from the same place, we decided to keep in touch by letter.
I first learned of Sretomorozsk's energy supply problems from a passing comment in one of her letters. Then, after her health went downhill, I started visiting more often to check in on her.
The town's been in decline for a while now. But because of her memory problems, she thinks of it as the bustling, prosperous Sretomorozsk, still in its heyday.
That said, I kinda appreciate her optimism. There's not much of it going around in this world of ice and snow.

dialogue.sit: Sorry, maybe I shouldn't have asked...

dialogue.t: It's fine. Everyone grows old.
In Snezhnaya, some people believe that in your final moments, you'll sense a familiar presence by your side.
You turn to look at them, but their face is blurry. So you focus hard, trying to make out who it is. When you finally see their face...
The Grim Reaper reaches out and takes your life.
She still calls me "grandson," though, so at least I'm not a blurry face in her world just yet.
C'mon, let's get back and see how Paimon's doing.

dialogue.sit: Paimon, we're back. Are you feeling any better?

dialogue.t: Yup, Paimon's not cold anymore, but she's still a little dizzy. Flying probably isn't a good idea right now — Paimon might lose her balance.
Hehe, but Paimon's sure she'll be fine. It's probably just from getting hit on the head by that pile of snow when we first arrived in Snezhnaya.
Her complexion's looking much better. Let's keep an eye on her.

dialogue.sit: I still think we should see a doctor when we get the chance.

dialogue.t: Sure. But enough about that — how did everything go on your end? Are you all set? Did you have any trouble?
I'll explain. It's a bit of a long story...
Geez, you guys got pretty busy! Sounds like the liaison officer and the mayor were running quite an operation... Hmph, good riddance to both of 'em. It's a good thing you managed to catch them.
So, you said the train station will open again soon, right? And everyone has enough Kristall now?
Yeah. Well, enough to survive, at least. Project Stuzha isn't going away any time soon. People will still have to scrimp and save to make ends meet.

dialogue.sit: I've been meaning to ask...
What exactly is the Tsaritsa trying to achieve?

dialogue.t: Don't know. The goal of Project Stuzha is to gather energy for the Tsaritsa, but no one knows where that energy's going. It's never been made public.
The thing is, we were told that the project would only last for six months. But time and time again, they keep extending it...
Extending it? Does that mean the Tsaritsa's plan isn't going very smoothly?
That's what everyone suspects. In principle, any proposed extension needs to pass by majority vote in the Snezhnograd Veche.
But even though opposition has been growing, any detractors end up caving in to political pressure from "The Rooster," Pulcinella.
He's the chair of the Snezhnograd Veche and a key figure in the voting process. He has the backing of many powerful and influential people.

dialogue.sit: Sounds like par for the course for the Fatui...

dialogue.t: How come the Fatui are picking on ordinary people even here in Snezhnaya?
I don't see it like that. Fundamentally, the Fatui will always think and act in the Tsaritsa's interests.

But that doesn't mean they don't care about the plight of the common folk. The only reason Sretomorozsk still receives Kristall shipments is because of a relief proposal put forward by The Rooster himself.

Then there's the Fatui soldiers providing support in every corner of the nation... Even the Northland Bank provided some Mora for disaster relief, and they're as conservative and indifferent as they come.
It's just that the rich and powerful in their fancy palaces live in a completely different world from us. There's always gonna be some conflict when those worlds collide.

dialogue.sit: I'm reminded of something that Fatui officer mentioned...
"The Rokot."

dialogue.t: Yeah, well, even though we all believe in Her Majesty the Tsaritsa, there are still many differences of opinion on how best to tackle the big issues of the day.
Regular folk don't have an easy way of getting their voices heard in Snezhnograd, while the rich and powerful are either unwilling or afraid to speak out for all sorts of complicated reasons.
"The Rokot" provides the disaffected with false identities and an outlet to vent their frustrations.
Of course, an organization like that exists in a gray area. The moment the Veche think they've crossed a line, there's sure to be a crackdown...
But so far, they've been doing their best to help the common folk.

dialogue.sit: They sound a lot like you.

dialogue.t: Like us, don't you mean? You didn't hesitate to join in. You're not new to this, I can tell.
That's 'cause we're adventurers! It's our job to help people out with commissions and get to the bottom of things.

dialogue.sit: It's less about the money...
...And more about the adventure itself.

dialogue.t: Sounds like we're going to get along.
So, what's your business in Snezhnograd? Aside from taking your friend to see a doctor, of course.

dialogue.sit: I want to meet the Tsaritsa. It's complicated... I've had run-ins with many of the Harbingers along the way, and I really need to know what the Tsaritsa is up to.
Her ultimate goal, what the Gnoses mean in all of this... Since I've made it this far in my journey, I have to find the truth, whatever it takes.

dialogue.t: Wait, so... No way. Are you... who I think you are?
Sounds like you've heard of us, then! Hehe, we're getting more famous by the day.

dialogue.sit: Of course, I know it won't be easy.
So I'm not planning to get there by force.

dialogue.t: I didn't realize I was in the company of giants.
Honestly, we're all as curious as you are about what the Tsaritsa's planning, and why it has to involve us freezing to death in the snow.

But getting in the same room as her won't be easy. The common folk aren't permitted to meet her at the best of times — and right now, she's probably not even in Snezhnograd. Word is, she's heading east on a campaign to slay a monster.

dialogue.sit: The one that's been summoning blizzards?

dialogue.t: Yeah. So you've heard of it. A wild, unpredictable monster with the power to summon snowstorms.
It also absorbs everything around it into its body, so it's growing constantly. Now, it's so big that the Tsaritsa has deemed it the number one threat.
Luckily, as it grew, it became increasingly less mobile, so it doesn't pose an immediate threat to this town or to Snezhnograd.
I'm sure the Tsaritsa and her personal guard, the Druzhna, won't have any trouble defeating the creature between them. It's just a question of how long it'll take...
Suffice to say, you won't be seeing her any time soon. You'll have to wait until she gets back.

dialogue.sit: That's fine. Getting Paimon treated is more urgent right now.
If it comes to it, I'll just have to go to her.

dialogue.t: Fair. Well, the Fatui will be taking over management of the train station for the time being. Things should be up and running by tomorrow.
Once it's open, we can see about getting your train towed to the station.
Whoa, that's gotta take a lot of manpower... Are you sure we can talk them into it?
The Fatui aren't exactly spotless in this whole mess, plus we helped them out. Should be easy enough to negotiate.

dialogue.sit: I'm more concerned about what paperwork I need to drive the train...

dialogue.t: As far as I know, all the paperwork is dealt with upon manufacture. I've never seen anyone check it, so I wouldn't worry.
Having a train makes everything much easier. We'll reach Snezhnograd in no time. I need to head there myself anyway — got some game to trade for Mora.
I know a good doctor in the city. I'll introduce you when we get there.
Thanks so much! Let's get a good night's sleep ahead of our big trip tomorrow.

dialogue.sit: After explaining the situation to the Fatui soldiers, they readily agree to help. Soon, the derailed train is back on the tracks.

dialogue.t: Drive carefully, alright? You don't wanna end up in this situation again.
...Also, I don't think I've seen a train like this before. Is it a new model or something?

dialogue.sit: Yeah, I guess.

dialogue.t: Hahaha, not a fan of small talk, are you? Anyway, take this — it's an up-to-date map of the Snezhnayan rail network.
All the track-switching is automated, so as long as the train's moving, you don't need to worry about collisions or anything.
We'll leave you to examine the train's conditions yourselves. Fingers crossed nothing's broken — I doubt Sretomorozsk has any engineers with experience working on this model.
Shouldn't be a problem. Thanks for everything.
Alright then. Have a safe journey, and make sure to check everything's working before you set off.
Alright, looks like our destination settings have been applied. Let's give this thing a final once-over and then head out. Goggles, your time to shine!

dialogue.sit: Over to you.

dialogue.t: Affirmative. Running vehicle diagnostics.
What's this?

dialogue.sit: Think of it as a kind of autopilot system.

dialogue.t: Engine: Green. Wheels: Green. Frame: ...Minor damage, but no impact on function.
Diagnostics complete. All systems nominal.
Neat! Paimon still can't get over the fact that you just found this tech lying around in a random cave.

dialogue.sit: Yeah, I definitely lucked out there...

dialogue.t: I've lived in Snezhnaya my whole life, and I've never heard of an interactive, talking train autopilot.
Strictly speaking, I wasn't designed purely to drive trains, though I doubt you have any interest in navigating the practically unreadable operator's manual yourself.
All configurations are complete. Should you require any further assistance, please call for the Eye of Graeae.

dialogue.sit: Thanks.

dialogue.t: Away we gooooo!
Nope, Paimon's gonna find a warmer seat...
Huh? What's going on?
Oh no!

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: ...Wh—What is this place? {NICKNAME}, are you okay?

dialogue.sit: I'm alright... You okay, Paimon?

dialogue.t: Uhh... Paimon's still airborne... But it feels like swimming through thick, gloopy water... Ugh, it's horrible...
Just our luck... Of all the things that could have gone wrong...
Alyosha, you're Snezhnayan right? Any idea what the heck this place is?

It's called the "Shadow Realm." A place where no wind blows, no light shines, and no elemental energy flows... even time itself doesn't exist here. It's a world where everything seems to come to a standstill.
I've only seen it a few times before, and this is my first time inside. It's a dangerous place. Most people who get sucked into the Shadow Realm are never seen again...
And the few who do make it back... They're never quite the same.
Huh? Then... What the heck do we do now?
Oh, maybe Goggles knows something. ...Goggles?

dialogue.sit: I don't see it anywhere...

dialogue.t: Great, now we're done for...
Hold it together. Let's not get ahead of ourselves. I heard a story once about the "World of Shadows"... If it's true, there's a way to escape. We just need to find the exit.
C'mon. Let's explore.
Wait, what's that blue thing? Is that... Goggles?
Guess we'd better find a way over.
Goggles!
Hello. I am glad to see the three of you safe and sound.
For now, at least. But things aren't looking too good.
Correct. We are now inside what is known as the Shadow Realm — the darkest space in the shell, where even the most high is loath to cast its gaze.
Time and space hold no meaning here. It intersects with the world of the Light Realm only rarely, like an air bubble that rises to the water's surface.
We must leave this place before it sinks back down into the depths once more.
Sounds like you have a plan.
...Yes. In fact, the very purpose of my creation was likely to... ... ...from the Shadow Realm.
...It appears that key data is currently inaccessible. But now is not the time to resolve that problem.
I have marked the exit to the Shadow Realm for your convenience. In addition, I have prepared some equipment to aid you as you traverse the Shadow Realm, {NICKNAME}...

dialogue.sit: There's specialist equipment for this?
How do you have that at the ready?

dialogue.t: It may well be one of my core functions... Scan complete. Construction in progress...
Activation code: "We once peered into the past from the ruins of the shadows. This is what remains of the Golden City, Hyperborea."

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: Whoa!
"Now go, arm yourselves with weapons of the spirit, bring down the walls of the stronghold, and extinguish the flaming arrows of the wicked."
Is this... a gun?
In the Shadow Realm, where humans cannot channel the elements... There once was one who, after much research and many attempts, found this to be the most effective means of attack.
Let's go, we don't have much time.
Many hostile units approaching...
I suggest a new strategy: Take cover, and pick them off one by one.
Huh, how do we get over there now?
I recommend using this Grappling Gun. Such devices were originally used to secure structures in the Shadow Realm.
If you detach the connected Hook, the Grappling Gun will automatically fire a rope to another nearby Hook...
Kay... So we just remove this hook, right?
Huh? W—Why is everything shaking so much?
Looks like the Shadow Realm is about to "sink back down into the depths."
The exit is right here...
You mean this... this weird bubble thing? ...Wait, um, how exactly do we—
No time to think — we just gotta go for it...
Whew... Looks like I was right!

dialogue.sit: After you successfully leave the Shadow Realm, the Eye of Graeae renovates the train at Rankova Zorya. Now, you can head to Snezhnograd.

dialogue.t: I can't believe the Shadow Realm manifested right on the railroad tracks. It's almost unheard of...
Lucky we made it out. All thanks to you and that awesome gun.

dialogue.sit: While we were in there, you mentioned Hyperborea...

dialogue.t: Ah, so you have heard of the Golden City before?
Yeah, it came up a whole bunch in Nod-Krai. You're a pretty neat surprise in that sense, aren't ya, Goggles? We had no idea they left cool gadgets like you behind.

dialogue.sit: Thanks for saving us again, Eye of Graeae.

dialogue.t: Make no mistake, it was a team effort. For a first-time firearm user, your performance was quite outstanding. Far beyond my expectations.
As Alyosha said, it is highly unusual for the Shadow Realm to manifest in a place like this. But we should still watch out for similar dangers ahead.
Let's hope not... If anything else goes wrong with this trip, Paimon's gonna have train-trauma for life...
The Shadow Realm can appear anywhere, not just on the railroad. I am simply advising that we take sensible precautions.
Now, if you wish to further calibrate and upgrade your firearm, you may do so over there, provided you have the necessary components.
Please take a moment to catch your breath while I repair the body of the train. Amongst other things, this will ensure Paimon is a little warmer while onboard.
Thanks, Goggles! You're a trusty train conductor. ...Uh, well maybe "trusty" isn't quite the right word, considering... Anyway, at least you get the job done!

dialogue.sit: So the gun can be upgraded?

dialogue.t: Yes, of course. And just like the Eye of Graeae, I am sure it will be a great asset to you in your future adventures — if not the trustiest, then it will at least get the job done.
Let's get some fresh air while the Eye of Graeae fixes the train.

dialogue.sit: Will you be okay, Paimon?

dialogue.t: Yeah, sure. Paimon wants to forget all about the Shadow Realm — it was so creepy in there. Stretching our legs might help take our mind off things.
It's so quiet here for a train station... Not a person in sight, just abandoned houses.
Huh!? So much for "repair"... You've swapped our train out for a whole new model!

My plan was to restore the train to its original appearance per my records as quickly as possible. Now that the repairs are complete, the train offers optimized performance and a significantly improved "trendiness" level.
Didn't know "trendiness" was a parameter...
According to my calculations, parameterization is the most effective way for the Eye of Graeae to understand trendiness.
("Hyperborea," huh? I'm sure I've heard of that in a story somewhere... What an incredible little gadget you are.)

quests.description: After several twists and turns, you finally reach the vicinity of Sretomorozsk via somewhat unorthodox means…

quests.title: Great Deeds on the Tundra

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: Here we are. Welcome to Snezhnograd train station — the biggest transport hub in the nation.
Wow, it's so majestic! Just flying from one side to the other would probably leave Paimon out of breath...
Heh, it's built for maximum efficiency. But yes, transferring trains here can be a little tiring.
In the future, you can use this train station to travel anywhere you want in Snezhnaya. For now, though, come with me. Let's get Paimon checked out.
This way. There's a lift car that goes straight to Zapolyarny.
Wow, Snezhnograd is stunning... Seeing it with our own eyes makes all the trouble we went through to get here worth it.
I found it pretty stunning when I first came here, too. But I soon found out that stunningly beautiful means stunningly expensive... The prices here are crazy.
I'm just a small-time hunter, so Zolnyy is where I spend most of my time.
This way will take us to Podvorye Restaurant. They offer food and lodging there, so you can get settled in while I fetch the doctor.
Um... is that gonna be stunningly expensive too...?

dialogue.sit: Don't you worry about that.
Keeping you warm and comfortable is all that matters.

dialogue.t: Yeah... I mean, there are places to stay in Zolnyy, but I highly doubt they'd meet your standards.
Most of the stoves are out of Kristall, the windows are drafty... and at night, four-legged roommates come out to play, sharpening their claws on the roof beams and floorboards.
Yep, no way. Not a chance Paimon's staying anywhere like that... Maybe we can split the cost of the room between us? Paimon still has some savings left.

dialogue.sit: What happened to sponging off me? Come on, it's tradition.

dialogue.t: Hmph, fine then! It's your treat! Paimon will save her money for buying a nice little cake...
...Don't worry, you'll get some too.
I'm glad to see you've perked up.
If you find yourselves in the mood for some sightseeing later, there's a few places around here worth seeing.
This way leads to Zapolyarny Palace, which serves as the Tsaritsa's audience chamber and also her personal quarters.
The adjacent block is kind of a city in its own right. That's Glupov, the headquarters of the Fatui.
Inside, there's a munitions factory known as the "Armory Palace" producing a constant supply of all kinds of equipment for the Fatui. A lot of important research happens there, too.
And over there is the Snezhnograd Veche, where all the big shots meet regularly to make policy decisions.
These places are best admired from a distance. I'm sure I don't need to explain why.
Yeah, they probably have super strict security. We're not looking for trouble right now.
The downtown area is near the center of Zapolyarny. That's where you'll find the restaurants, bookstores, and gift shops.
Another place of interest is the Northland Bank, which is over this way.
Oh, and I'm sure you'll want to make contact with the Adventurers' Guild at some point, right? That's right here.
Ooh, speaking of adventuring, we use alchemy quite a lot. D'you know where we can find a Crafting Bench?
Um... No one practices alchemy in Snezhnograd, I'm afraid. Apparently, there's some historical reason for it.
Oh. We'll just have to use the one on the train, then... *sigh* Kinda inconvenient. ...Wait, how come there's one on the train if that's Snezhnayan too?

dialogue.sit: Yeah, that's weird...
Maybe we can look into the "historical reasons" later.

dialogue.t: Yeah, I dunno. Not my area of expertise. Still, I wouldn't say the absence of alchemy makes life here any less convenient.
Anyway — finally, there's Zolnyy in that direction. It's mostly residential buildings and factories, but there's a few shops too. Worth a look around if you're interested.
That's about it. You guys go ahead and get checked in while I track down my doctor friend.
Sounds good. Thanks for all the recommendations. It'll be good to get out of the cold wind — Paimon's starting to feel another headache coming on.

dialogue.sit: Let's get you inside.

dialogue.t: Podvorye Restaurant is right this way.

dialogue.sit: After checking in, you and Paimon arrive at your room.

dialogue.t: Looks like you get what you pay for, huh! Paimon likes this room a lot!

dialogue.sit: Feeling better now?

dialogue.t: Yeah, much better now that we're out of the cold. Thanks for taking such good care of Paimon. Honestly, she feels kinda bad for throwing a wrench in the works...
If this were anywhere else, we'd be out investigating and adventuring by now. But instead, we're stuck here waiting for a doctor.

dialogue.sit: It's okay. We aren't under any time pressure.
The sooner you recover, the sooner we can start exploring.

dialogue.t: ...You're right. No need to push ourselves too hard for no reason.
A lot happened on our way into the city. Let's review what we've learned so far and try to figure out what to do next.
Obviously, the million-Mora question is: "What is the Tsaritsa planning?" Everything else leads back to that.

dialogue.sit: Yeah, that was our main goal in coming to Snezhnaya.

dialogue.t: Sure was. And so far, we've learned that in addition to the seven Gnoses, her plan also requires a ton of energy.
But we won't get to see her anytime soon. Alyosha said that she went east to fight that big monster.
It must be a pretty powerful one if it can blanket the whole of Snezhnaya in a snowstorm this awful.

dialogue.sit: Mm-hmm. It's one of the threats we'll need to face, I think.

dialogue.t: ...To be honest, what we're really lacking right now is information. The kind of information that only the higher-ups in the government would know, not "word-on-the-street" type of info.
Paimon can think of a few people who might be able to help us, but...

dialogue.sit: They're all Fatui.

dialogue.t: Right. And when we left Nod-Krai, Sandrone specifically left a message reminding us which side we're on...
So it's unlikely they'd tell us anything confidential about the Tsaritsa's grand plan.

dialogue.sit: It's still worth asking.
Maybe we can learn some non-confidential info.

dialogue.t: Yeah, fair point. Besides, that Glupov place is right nearby. We've got nothing to lose, so it'd be a waste not to go.
There's gotta be someone there willing to talk to us, right? Maybe Arlecchino or Sandrone... Hmm, or possibly Tartaglia.
But it's unlikely we could sweet-talk Arlecchino. Let alone Sandrone... she basically told us to stay in our lane already.

dialogue.sit: Well, it's been a while since we last saw Tartaglia.

dialogue.t: Yeah, the last time was all the way back in Fontaine, right? Too bad we missed him in Nod-Krai. Apparently, he came to help out.
Hello, is there a {NICKNAME} and Paimon in there?
That's Alyosha! Come in!
Hello, I'm Doctor Luneva. Alyosha mentioned that one of you is feeling a little under the weather?

dialogue.sit: We'd be grateful if you could take a look at her.

dialogue.t: I see. So you're my patient today, yes? And you're a... fae, I presume?
Good question... Paimon's not too sure either, but she's definitely not the same kind of fae as the ones we saw at the train station. ...Is that gonna be an issue?
Not exactly, it's just... I'm used to treating human patients. Fae tend to be far more resilient than even the healthiest and most long-lived of humans.
But don't worry, I do have some experience treating fae. I've even diagnosed plenty of cats and dogs in my time. Safe to say, I have a fairly eclectic range of expertise.
It'll be fine! Paimon's basically the same as a human.
Right? We're no different when it comes down to it, are we?

dialogue.sit: Our taste in food is a little different.
The biggest difference is probably your appetite...

dialogue.t: Hmph! That's just 'cause Paimon knows how to eat!
Hehe. Now, please take a seat.
Okay, vital signs are good, test results are all within normal ranges... I don't think it's anything serious. More than likely, you've just caught a cold.
I can give you some medicine to tide you over, but as long as you rest properly for the next couple of days, you should feel better. Make sure to keep an eye on your temperature, though.
If you find yourself with a persistent low-grade fever or if your symptoms don't improve, just contact me again.
Sounds like there's no cause for alarm.

dialogue.sit: Yeah. Let's see how it goes over the next few days.

dialogue.t: Thank you, Doctor.
You're very welcome. Just doing my job. I'll leave you in peace now — time to visit my next patients.
Take care.
You heard the doctor. Best you rest up here for a couple days. No sightseeing for the time being.

dialogue.sit: I'll stick to the local area, then.
Don't you worry about that.

dialogue.t: Alright then, guess we've got no choice. Let's just treat it as a short vacation!
I have to get back to it. If you need anything else from the doctor or me, go to the Hunter Trade Station in Zolnyy. The boss there knows how to reach me.

dialogue.sit: Thanks for everything.

dialogue.t: Hey, no big deal. You saved my life in the Shadow Realm. This is the least I could do. See ya around.
Hold on. Please display your invitation letter or permit.

dialogue.sit: I'm looking for someone.
Could you pass along the message?

dialogue.t: Glupov does not accept meeting requests without a prior appointment. You'll have to apply per the advertised booking process and wait until your invitation letter is issued.

dialogue.sit: But we're old friends.
I know they'll want to see me.

dialogue.t: ...Might I ask who you're hoping to visit?

dialogue.sit: Harbinger "Childe," Tartaglia.

dialogue.t: (Another one who thinks the rules don't apply to them... I don't understand why people think they can talk their way in here. You don't just show up and land a meeting with a Harbinger...)
(Ugh, but I have to go through the motions, for protocol's sake. Honestly, it's such a waste of time asking when I already know what the answer's gonna be.)
Wait a moment — I'll pass on your message. If Childe is unavailable, you'll have to go through the proper procedure.

dialogue.sit: After a slightly awkward wait outside Glupov with an unimpressed Fatui guard, there is still no sign of Tartaglia.

dialogue.t: Lord Childe is a busy man. He's probably not in Glupov at present. If I were you, I'd cut your losses. No point waiting any longer.

dialogue.sit: Guess I picked a bad time.

dialogue.t: Even if you two are old friends as you claim, please understand that the Fatui Harbingers are often busy with their official duties. They tend not to stay at Glupov for extended periods.
Next time, stick to the rules. You'll make life easier for both of us... Hmm?
Greetings, Lady Marionette.

dialogue.sit: Sandrone?

dialogue.t: I'll take care of our guest here. It's his(her) first time in Snezhnaya, so it's no surprise that he(she) doesn't know the rules yet.
I trust no choice words have been exchanged? No misunderstandings I should be aware of?
No, Lady Marionette. No incidents to report.
(Phew, that was a close call... Good thing I played it cool...)

dialogue.sit: I'm the one who showed up unannounced...
This gentleman has been very accommodating.

dialogue.t: Is that right? Good to know. Hmm... wait, where's Paimon?

dialogue.sit: She's a little under the weather.
She's recovering at Podvorye Restaurant.

dialogue.t: Under the weather? Huh, that's hard to imagine. She's always buzzing with energy...
I take it she's still adapting to the climate? Happens to a lot of people. It's even colder here than in Nod-Krai. Has she seen a doctor? I can get you one if you need.

dialogue.sit: She's already seen a doctor. She said it's nothing serious.
She just needs to rest for a couple of days.

dialogue.t: Alright then. Well, let me know if you run into any other problems.

dialogue.sit: Did you come out here specifically to see me?

dialogue.t: Why else? I was just about to sit down for some much-needed tea time when I heard that an old friend of Tartaglia's had shown up outside, no appointment, nothing.

And, as obnoxious as it may be to show up uninvited at Glupov, I couldn't help but take pity on the poor soul who was waiting outside in vain. So, I had no choice but to abandon my freshly brewed, piping-hot tea and come to see this mystery guest for myself...

dialogue.sit: You already guessed it was me, didn't you?

dialogue.t: Hmph. Well, I felt our time working together in Nod-Krai warranted some courtesy. I couldn't exactly let you freeze to death out here in the wind.
Unfortunately, I can't invite you inside either. The rules of Glupov wouldn't allow it, and as a Harbinger, I have to lead by example.
On the plus side, Snezhnograd actually has some class — unlike Nasha Town. Torchlight Books has a very nice selection of teas and cakes, so we can catch up there.
Your treat, of course.

dialogue.sit: What? Why?

dialogue.t: Because I already wasted one perfectly good cup of tea today. That's why.
I've ordered for the both of us. No objections, I assume? I'm sure you trust my taste.

dialogue.sit: No problem...
(Though I'm sure you mostly ordered for yourself...)

dialogue.t: Okay, let's get down to business. I'm guessing you don't actually have any urgent business with Tartaglia, per se. You just want information, right?

dialogue.sit: Yup, you got it... But how's he doing, anyway?
What's he been up to lately?

dialogue.t: Wanna take a guess?

dialogue.sit: Um... Has he been picking fights again?

dialogue.t: Heh, of course you'd say that. You shouldn't underestimate Councilor Tartaglia, you know...

dialogue.sit: "Councilor"?

dialogue.t: That's right. I'm sure you've heard of the Snezhnograd Veche by now? Well, he's busy preparing some paperwork for their next meeting.
They'll be discussing yet another extension to Project Stuzha. It's basically all anyone cares about in the Veche these days.

dialogue.sit: Tartaglia, a councilor... Sorry, it's just a little hard to imagine...
He doesn't exactly strike me as pen-pusher.

dialogue.t: Yeah, he's more of the "shoot first, ask questions later" sort, isn't he?
It all started with a very detailed letter that Capitano left for "The Jester," Pierro, before leaving for Natlan.
In that letter, he detailed the future arrangements for his subordinates. All of his key people were reassigned to Tartaglia.
I guess he'd already prepared to leave us for good all the way back then. But Pierro didn't reveal the contents of the letter until the events in Natlan had concluded.

dialogue.sit: Why Tartaglia?

dialogue.t: Heh, that was his reaction, too. "Why me," with a bewildered look on his face.
He'd always assumed Capitano looked down on him. He was a man who kept his thoughts to himself and barely spoke to him the whole time they'd known each other.
But he occasionally brought Tartaglia along to my tea parties back in the day. So to the rest of us, it was clear that Capitano had quite a lot of respect for his young comrade.
...By "the rest of us," I mean my tea party regulars: Arlecchino, Rosalyne, and... actually, not Columbina. She was probably oblivious to it.

Anyway, then the Liyue situation happened... Normally, it took a lot to get under Capitano's skin, but that time he was furious... It's not really my place to talk about it, though. You can ask Tartaglia about it sometime.
Basically, Tartaglia probably had the wrong idea about Capitano all along, right up until Pierro revealed the letter he'd left behind.
Capitano believed that despite Tartaglia's immaturity, he showed great potential — plus, he possessed a kind of purity rarely seen among members of the Fatui.

dialogue.sit: That makes sense.

dialogue.t: Yeah, it's one of the few things that I'd agree those two have in common. But there's one other reason why Capitano chose Tartaglia to assume command of his troops.
He knew that after he was gone, several of the others would swoop in on his army like vultures...
With the ones who stood to benefit the most being "The Rooster," Pulcinella, and "Regrator," Pantalone.
Once they'd divided Capitano's troops between them, they'd be more powerful than ever. No one would be able to stop them...
...So, you can see why Capitano chose to hand that letter to Pierro, right?

dialogue.sit: Because The Jester needs to maintain a balance of power?

dialogue.t: Exactly. Pierro also needed to back a Harbinger as soon as possible. And all things considered, Tartaglia was the best choice.
Even though Tartaglia has had the support of Northland Bank for a long time, he and Pantalone are ultimately not cut from the same cloth.
I'd say Capitano made a good judgment call. Anyone else caught in this situation would probably feel like they'd been hung out to dry.
His best course of action will be to distance himself from any shady business while still maintaining friendly relations with Pantalone, but seeking Pulcinella's support at the same time.

dialogue.sit: Are you sure it's okay to tell me all this inside information?

dialogue.t: Heh, what's the point in having a tea party if you don't spill a little tea?
Besides, none of this is confidential anyway. Ask any journalist out there — they'll give you all the lurid details.
You'll see it firsthand if you ever sit in on a session of the Snezhnograd Veche. All the factional strife, whether open or unspoken — it plays out for all to see in that one little room.
Having a voice in the Veche is the only way to steer policies in your favor. So, every person in that room represents a particular interest group.
Pantalone, for instance, represents the financial sector, and Tartaglia represents the Fatui soldiers.
Personally, I have no interest in political jousting, but since I have a number of engineers and researchers under my command, I have to make their voices heard.
Then there's Pulcinella, the linchpin of the Veche. He represents "politics" itself.
Everything involves him, so nothing can bypass him. Any issue that comes up, he knows how to mediate. That's what the Tsaritsa values most about him.

dialogue.sit: This explains a lot...
(I'm starting to see why everyone is so frustrated with the way things are, but also powerless to change it...)
(A complex web of interests connects all parties involved, and the Tsaritsa sitting at the top adds another layer of complexity. It must be nearly impossible to come up with a perfect solution.)

dialogue.t: Alright, I'm done carrying this conversation. Time for you to answer a question of mine.
You must have known that you can get the info you needed from me. So why was Tartaglia the first person you asked to see, and not me?

dialogue.sit: What makes you ask that?
You're not... jealous, are you?

dialogue.t: I just don't understand, that's all. Anyway, do I really need a reason?
Wait... Oh, I think I know what it is... Columbina passed on my message to you before you left Nod-Krai, right?
I only meant you should be mindful of which side you're on... Is that actually why you didn't ask for me? Because you took that to heart?

dialogue.sit: I guess that's part of the reason.
I wanted to make sure I wasn't being disrespectful...

dialogue.t: You...! Ugh, fair enough, it's not your fault. I blame all these politicians I've been hanging around with lately. Always beating about the bush when they talk — I guess it must've rubbed off on me...
Anyway, just ask for my help next time, okay? Little things like this are no problem.
Lady Marionette.
What now? Can't you see I'm on my break!? Whatever it is, just leave it on my desk! I'll look at it later...
Sorry to disturb you during your break, Ma'am, but I'm afraid it's an emergency...
Ugh, isn't it always? I've told you before: Fixing the tracks and transporting ice blocks does not constitute an emergency...
The equipment in Svetloledovka is in urgent need of maintenance. With how the weather's been recently, we suspect that the cause is a buildup of snow, exceeding the maximum weight limit.
The supports on one of the machines broke and fell, awakening a dormant beast and leaving many of the ice miners trapped in a nearby ice cave.
Luckily, Odette's team was nearby and launched a rescue operation. But we're still facing a severe manpower shortage for both the rescue and engineering teams.
I guess that's it, then. Our tea party will have to end here. I'm the only engineer you'll need.

dialogue.sit: I kinda wanna go with you...
But I promised Paimon I wouldn't go too far.

dialogue.t: Do you actually want to come with, or are you just saying that?

dialogue.sit: I owe you for the "tea" you shared with me.
I can't just stand by when people are in danger.

dialogue.t: Hmph. Nice of you to return the favor... I'll have a couple of people look after Paimon. They can let her know that you had to step out for a while. Given how urgent this is, I'm sure she'll understand.
And honestly, I'd rather have your help than anyone else's. Between your skills and experience, you'd be reliable help.

dialogue.sit: Great, thanks. Sounds like a plan.

dialogue.t: Then let's go. You, take two people to Podvorye Restaurant. Find his(her) room and watch it like a hawk until we get back.
If anything happens to Paimon, you'll be answering to me.
Yes, Lady Marionette!
They weren't exaggerating — this is really dangerous. It's a good thing only one of them broke...
From what I've been told, most of the trapped miners are over in that direction.

dialogue.sit: I'll go rescue them.

dialogue.t: Yeah, you do that while I check the rest of the equipment. I'll evacuate the people around here as I go.
Meet me back here as soon as you're done.

dialogue.sit: (I have to be getting close...)

dialogue.t: Don't go any further.
It's too dangerous here. There's a highly aggressive monster on the prowl. You need to leave, now.

dialogue.sit: I'm here to help with the rescue effort.
I'm with Sandrone.

dialogue.t: Ah, I see — you're the backup from Snezhnograd. Well, I'm Odette. Good to meet you.

dialogue.sit: (Ah, so this is Odette. She was the first member of the Fatui on the scene...)

dialogue.t: There are five people trapped in the cave. Monster type is unknown, and so is its location.
Let's go, every second counts.
Thank you for saving us... We'd have been monster-fodder otherwise.
Thank you, thank you...
Welcome. You should be safe now. Follow this route out. He(She) and I will stay behind to watch the rear.

dialogue.sit: The path's been cleared.
It's safe now.

dialogue.t: Thank you... C'mon, let's go. This way.
I've searched the area. Pretty sure the monster made a tactical retreat.

dialogue.sit: Was this its lair?

dialogue.t: Yeah, but with us here, it won't be coming back anytime soon.
It may be small, but don't be fooled — it's a ferocious beast. People are just food in its eyes...
It's lucky we got here when we did.
The trapped miners have been successfully evacuated. Time for us to leave.

dialogue.sit: Wait, this place... There's something unusual about it...
(Cutscene, Escape from the ice cave)
After escaping the cave, the monster finally gives up the chase. With the rescue complete, you return safe and sound to Svetloledovka...

dialogue.t: Everyone's accounted for — we managed to rescue them all. We also placed a sign at the entrance to the cave, warning people to stay away.
...You really held your own today. I... still don't know your name.

dialogue.sit: It's {NICKNAME}. I'm an adventurer.

dialogue.t: Hmm. Don't think I've seen you before. I'll remember the name.
Alright then... see you around.
Hello, Lady Marionette.
I hear the rescue operation was a great success. I knew I could count on you.
What brings you here, Odette? Here for a performance?
No, a Fatui mission. I happened to be nearby and heard the crash.

dialogue.sit: Performance?

dialogue.t: She hasn't introduced herself, then. Hehe, Odette is the prima ballerina of Snezhnograd. She's quite the celebrity.
If you ever hear people mention the "two crowning jewels of the Korolevskiy Troupe," they're talking about Odette and the prima donna, Vodyanitsa.
On top of that, Odette's also a rising Fatui star. It's looking likely she'll inherit the title of "The Fair Lady."
She learned all her combat skills from Rosalyne herself. Used to be one of her most valued subordinates, too.
...You flatter me, Lady Marionette.

dialogue.sit: (If she's Rosalyne's protegee, that makes me... Never mind, there's no need to bring it up. No point making things awkward.)
N—No wonder you're such a keen fighter...

dialogue.t: How's progress on your end, Lady Marionette?
Equally successful — I've finished reinforcing all the equipment. Took me a little longer without Pulonia's help... Hmph, but the outcome is the same, of course.
Even if the heavy snowfall summoned by that monster lasts for another three months straight, this equipment won't give way.
Alright — now that we're done here, it's time to get out of this blizzard.

dialogue.sit: That's it? Isn't there more work to be done here?

dialogue.t: Sure, but Snezhnograd will send someone to investigate and draw up a relief plan... Ugh, and I guess I'll have to write the incident report myself this time, since it involves a mechanical malfunction.
First, Pantalone needs to approve the budget, then Pulcinella has to sign off on the plan. Once they've argued it out and reached a compromise, we can move forward...
That's the rough process, anyway. Could take anywhere from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, depending on how smoothly it goes.

dialogue.sit: And in the meantime, the people here just have to wait?

dialogue.t: Yup. Nothing we can do about it. There's a whole stack of incident reports like this back at the office.

dialogue.sit: (The snow has eased a little for now, but there's no telling when that will change with that monster still at large...)
(Fuel for heating is in short supply, and relief is weeks away. There's no immediate threat to life, but still...)
(It just feels like there should be a better way.)

dialogue.t: Hey, quit daydreaming. Let's get back to Snezhnograd.
Ah. Well, if it isn't Councilor Tartaglia. Mr. Big Shot himself.
Heh, go easy on me, alright? I'm still recovering from the interrogation the real big shots put me through.
Hey, comrade. It's been too long! I heard you came looking for me earlier. Nicest surprise I've had in a while.
Good to see you too, Odette. I'm guessing you guys just got back from Svetloledovka? How'd it go? Crisis averted?
It went fine.
How about you? Any new developments?
Not really, same as ever. Growing opposition to Project Stuzha, and the usual rebuttals are starting to ring hollow.
The results of the mock vote were pretty dire. Pulcinella was fuming... I've never seen the old man so angry.
That's not good news... It takes a lot to rattle him.
Yeah. Obviously, if push comes to shove, there are ways to crack down on dissent, but...

dialogue.sit: Sorry, I have to ask something. This is going to sound blunt, but may I?

dialogue.t: Huh? Of course, fire away.

dialogue.sit: It sounds to me like everyone's tearing their hair out trying to figure out how to deal with opposition to Project Stuzha.
But what exactly is this project's purpose? And how can it be so important that even people like you two refuse to stand up for the ordinary people of Snezhnaya?

dialogue.t: (Haha. Interesting. I gotta hand it to you, comrade — you sure don't mince your words...)
(Excuse him(her)!? What does he(she) mean, refuse to stand up for ordinary people!?)
(Oh my gosh... How does he(she) dare speak to the Harbingers like that?)
Are you interrogating us now?
It's okay, Sandrone. Let me explain. I think I understand where he(she)'s coming from.
...If I could, I'd take your side right now.
In fact, my position's very similar to yours. I've only held back on casting a dissenting vote in the Veche because the Tsaritsa would never let me get away with it.
Still, I have a responsibility to the Fatui armed forces, so I do what I can to make their voices heard. Most of them are just regular folks from small towns far from the capital.
I'm sure you've seen how much those kinds of places are struggling right now. Oh, and for what it's worth, I'm from Morepesok myself. Things aren't going so swell there, either.

dialogue.sit: Right, so this affects you directly. Hence my question.

dialogue.t: The Tsaritsa wants to create a better, safer future for the people of Snezhnaya, but she's thinking long-term. I don't doubt that from where you're standing, Project Stuzha seems to be creating all sorts of issues for everyone.
But considering the Tsaritsa's vision for the future, these are sacrifices worth making. Sounds cold, I know. But I promise it's not as black-and-white as it seems.
Maybe Sandrone and I can't oppose Project Stuzha outright, but we're constantly raising our concerns in Veche meetings.
And even though we can't put an end to it, there are plenty of other ways to make a difference. We're trying everything we can think of, and so is Pulcinella.
I respect Her Majesty the Tsaritsa and trust her decisions. But at the end of the day, I'm still just a normal guy who cares deeply about my homeland... and my family, who all live here.
There's no way I would ever abandon them.
As contentious as things can get within the Veche, there's no selfishness or malice behind it. Everyone wants to get through this period as smoothly as possible.
The issue is that there's no way of pleasing everyone under the present circumstances. Most of the time, we're trying to decide on the lesser of two evils, which obviously isn't a great look.

But that is not the same thing as being blindly loyal to the Tsaritsa. No one's got their head in the sand here. We're all well aware of the way things are — we're just doing our best to make it work.

dialogue.sit: (In fairness to Sandrone, she rushed to Svetloledovka's aid the moment she heard that people were in danger.)
(And even Tartaglia, who used to only care about the thrill of the fight, is clearly doing his best to rise to the demands of his new role as councilor...)
Sorry, maybe my question was a bit rude.
But I'd still like to know what exactly the Tsaritsa is up to...

dialogue.t: Hey, come on. There's only so much we can say, so don't press us too hard. Look, I know how untenable the Tsaritsa's position looks if you don't understand her motives.
Maybe you've heard already, but she's currently leading her army on a campaign to the east to defeat the monster that's been causing these brutal blizzards.
Striking that monster down will be a significant step in dealing with the present energy crisis.
As laser-focused as she is on realizing her lifelong ambitions, she's still putting time and energy into taking down this powerful monster.
To me, that says a lot. If she thought Snezhnaya and its people didn't matter in the grand scheme of things, why would she waste her time on something like this?

dialogue.sit: You have a point...
You've become quite the smooth talker.

dialogue.t: Haha, thanks. I meant every word I said, though. I wasn't just trying to placate you — I've already done more than enough diplomacy for one day.
...I still think this adventurer raises a very important point.
Our two Harbingers have made their positions very clear. But there are many others in the Veche who must feel trapped and forced to vote against their conscience.
I think it's a very valuable quality to be willing to speak one's mind despite the risk of offending powerful figures.

dialogue.sit: It's mostly because we know each other quite well...

dialogue.t: Hmph, you can say that again. I highly doubt we'd feel the need to explain ourselves so much if we didn't know you so well.
Forgive me, Adventurer, but might I be so bold as to ask about your background? How is it that you can converse so openly with two Harbingers?
Umm...
Oh, haven't you been properly introduced?
Easier said than done... I like to think I'm not the kind of person who goes around busting open people's old wounds!
I've only learned his(her) name so far, no details of his(her) experiences. Is... something wrong?

dialogue.sit: (Uh oh... is there no avoiding the subject of Rosalyne...?)

dialogue.t: No, it's just... *sigh* Alright, I guess there's no getting around it.
This is the world-renowned Traveler, who helped resolve the Stormterror threat in Mondstadt, cleaned up after the mess I made in Liyue... and then went to Inazuma, where...
...There was a duel before the throne, in which the Traveler defeated Rosalyne.
Oh...
I'm sorry, I didn't think you two would be seeing much of each other, so I figured it wasn't worth bringing up...
It's fine, it was a long time ago... It's fine.
Sorry, I just remembered that we have a rehearsal coming up. Please excuse me, I should get going.
*sigh*
I've mentioned this to you before, remember? She was Rosalyne's most valued subordinate... but they didn't actually get along.
Not that Rosalyne was really the type of person to make friends, but... death has a way of resolving a lot of conflicts.
Don't let it weigh on you. Like she said, it was a long time ago. It's in the past now.
